title: [MIG-003] Seed Vibez from a reproducible, provenance-recorded workflow export
objective: Give Vibez its own buildable source, tests and governance without altering Fantasy Football's running workflows.
inScope: Use MIG-001's seed protocol and MIG-002's allowlist. Select a current accepted source SHA (planning baseline fbc46888ce0bd2af454f471561911a913d32e6fc is not permission to ignore later fixes). Export implementation, schemas, contracts, selected reusable docs/scripts and tests into Vibez. Preserve the UAT fix from source #76 and automated canary/adversarial coverage; fixture tests are not live acceptance.

Record source SHA, path/blob hashes, mapping, destination seed SHA and justified transformations. Retain historical commits/issues in the source repository using immutable links rather than rewriting history or importing its full bootstrap state.

Install destination governance, build/test/schema CI and development instructions appropriate to Vibez. Handle schema/contract validation tooling explicitly; distinguish development Python requirements from runtime requirements.
Exclude credentials, ignored .agent state, exchanges, worktrees, historical live approvals and unrelated project content. Do not seed a lifecycle by copying source DONE/assignment records.

Maintain a source-delta ledger for #78 and required bug fixes until the final synchronization checkpoint. Baseline reusable implementation is owned in Vibez after export; source exceptions must be explicitly tracked and reconciled once.
**Expected surfaces:** Approved source/schema/contract/test/docs/script tree, package/build metadata, destination governance, .github/workflows and provenance/export tooling.
outOfScope: No source deletion, history rewriting, brand-driven schema migration, public package publication or runtime-state transfer.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-01: A clean Vibez checkout builds and runs inherited tests, schema/contract checks and adversarial checks independently of the Fantasy Football checkout.
AC-02: An automated inventory/provenance comparison accounts for every included, excluded and intentionally transformed path.
AC-03: Artifact/working-tree scan finds no credentials, live runtime data, stopped canary exchange or unrelated project content.
AC-04: UAT requirements/affected/dependency-contract regressions and current workflow guarantees survive export.
AC-05: Destination CI, licensing decision references and the delta ledger are present; an extraction is not described as new independent review of historical source runs.
validationPlan:
Run destination build, full inherited tests, both schema validations and adversarial mutation checks. Reproduce the export into a fresh directory and compare mapping/content. Compare relevant source and destination behavior; record all environmental exceptions.

Use applicable repository build/test/schema/contract checks. Retain exact commands/results, package/source/config identities and an acceptance-to-evidence map. Existing or fake-provider fixtures are not independent live review or task-completion evidence. This task is normal feature work, not a new canary requirement.
npm run build; npm test; python schemas/validate_fixtures.py; python schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py; npm run test:adversarial:mutations. Add issue-specific checks before admission.
